research_result.description: Asana is a productivity and work management platform that offers a comprehensive REST API and an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for programmatic task, project, and workflow integration.
research_result.credential_requirements: Developers can self-serve credentials by creating Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or registering OAuth/MCP apps in the Asana Developer Console. For organization-wide access without user attribution, Service Accounts require an Enterprise tier plan and creation by an Asana super admin.

evidence.claim: Asana supports Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for programmatic REST API access.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: generating a PAT allows you to access (i.e., make requests to) the Asana REST API upon successful authentication.

evidence.claim: Asana supports OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow for authorizing third-party apps.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asana supports the authorization code grant flow

evidence.claim: Asana supports Service Accounts on Enterprise tiers for org-wide access.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Service Accounts (SAs) are long-lived tokens that provide programmatic access to the API. Service Accounts are an Enterprise tier feature and can only be created by Asana super admins
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON or form-encoded requests, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP features

evidence.claim: Asana provides an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, accessible via app integration, which allows AI assistants and other applications to access the Asana Work Graph from beyond the Asana platform.

evidence.claim: Developers can self-serve PATs and app creation via the Developer Console.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You can use the developer console to create apps and personal access tokens (PATs).
